cases.description: Two ordered samples in one UTC clock domain and boot epoch are coherent for review.
An exact duplicate packet with the same sample identity, sequence and payload digest is idempotent.
The same epoch sequence is reused with a conflicting payload digest.
Sequence 2 is missing even though the expected stream window contains three observations.
A late packet arrives out of receipt order but inside the declared bounded reorder window.
A late packet arrives beyond the declared reorder window.
A device sequence counter resets inside the same boot epoch without a declared epoch transition.
A reboot opens a new boot epoch and records the exact transition receipt.
A sequence counter wraps at its declared width under an explicit modulo policy.
The sequence counter width is unknown, so wrap and uniqueness cannot be reconstructed.
An NTP backward clock step occurs without a new epoch or qualified correction.
An NTP forward clock step occurs without a new epoch or qualified correction.
A monotonic counter resets inside the same epoch.
The sample clock source changes from NTP to PTP without a corresponding clock epoch.
Sample synchronization uncertainty exceeds the downstream purpose limit.
A sample is tagged in milliseconds while the stream contract is nanoseconds.
A sample is tagged in microseconds while the stream contract is seconds.
Two samples use different timestamp origins in the same stream.
A local-wall-time sample has no UTC offset or qualified mapping.
A repeated daylight-saving local hour lacks fold/offset disambiguation.
A local calendar instant falls in a skipped daylight-saving interval and is marked invalid.
The declared calendar instant is not a valid date/time.
The source contains a leap-second token unsupported by the declared parser/time mapping.
Subsecond precision was rounded away without a declared precision-loss allowance.
Collector receipt time is substituted for physical event time in a service aggregation.
Acquisition time precedes event time without a buffering or latency explanation.
A sample identity is reused with a different instrument identity.
The instrument serial identity was reused after replacement.
Firmware identity changes inside a supposedly homogeneous stream.
A clock-correction mapping is retrospectively rewritten after downstream use.
The verified clock-correction map validity interval does not cover all samples.
The residual clock-correction error exceeds its declared uncertainty.
A sample from an unrelated boot epoch is inserted without a declared reboot transition.
Sequence order and event-time order disagree, so the stream cannot be replayed consistently.
The declared observation schedule contains a packet-loss gap hidden by a favorable observed count.
Missing intervals are imputed as zero before a downstream aggregate is evaluated.
An integration window crosses an unresolved clock step.
A rate calculation uses collector receipt intervals rather than event-time intervals.
A different room's clock mapping changes; this stream and its raw samples must remain unaffected.
A clock mapping change invalidates only this stream's dependent aggregate while preserving raw samples and unrelated streams.
